messages:
alex: Heads up — we're planning to retire the legacy /v1/streaming endpoint at the end of Q2. Running a quick proposal: instead of forcing clients to upgrade overnight, we add a lightweight shim ("slim-bridge") that translates v1 -> v2 shapes with minimal mutating. Low overhead, per-tenant opt-in, short-lived.
marta: Can you outline what the shim actually does? is it full protocol emulation or just header/body rewrite?
alex: Short version: header passthrough + payload shape translation. It will handle these pieces:
- Accept incoming v1 SSE/WebSocket connections
- Translate v1 framing -> v2 chatstream frames (preserve token chunks)
- Map error codes and retry semantics
- Forward auth header to control plane for tenant config check
kevin: Streaming semantics are tricky. How do we handle backpressure and client-side chunking? we don't want the shim to buffer a whole response.
alex: Good call. Design constraint: no large buffers. shim operates as a proxy with an async passthrough stream. Only minimal mutation on the streaming frames (update meta fields). If downstream v2 sends backpressure, we propagate that back to the v1 socket.
shilpa: What about SSE vs WS differences? v1 clients use both.
alex: We'll support both at the shim edge. Internally we normalize to an internal event stream and then open a v2 stream to the runtime. On the way back we re-encode according to the original client transport (SSE/WS).
lia: Metrics/observability: we need token counts, per-tenant latency, and translation error counters. Also trace continuity (preserve request-id). Can we inject the same trace id into v2 calls?
kevin: Accepting and forwarding trace/request ids is fine. Add a "rw-compat" header so we can detect shim traffic in logs.
alex: Example minimal mapping in pseudo-config we'd run in the shim:
```
route {
  match: /v1/streaming
  transport: sse|ws
  transform: {
    frame_map: v1_chunk -> v2_delta.tokens
    error_map: 422 -> 400
  }
  headers: forward + inject ["x-request-id", "x-rw-compat"]
}
```
marta: Latency overhead? if this adds >5-10ms we break SLOs for some tenants.
alex: We expect ~1-3ms additional CPU hops on p95 with connection pooling and pinned worker threads. We'll bench this with a synthetic token stream (1k concurrent streams, avg 50 tokens/sec) before any rollout.
shilpa: Security: auth header forwarding needs to avoid leaking creds. We should validate tokens against control plane before proxying downstream.
alex: Agreed. Flow: shim accepts token, calls control plane auth-check (cached TTL 30s), then establishes downstream connection with a shim-managed service token. No upstream creds forwarded to runtime.
lia: Rollout plan idea: 1) shadow mode (no rewrites, just metrics) for 2 weeks, 2) opt-in per-tenant header flag, 3) small canary (5 tenants), 4) gradual ramp. add an emergency kill-switch.
kevin: Forwards: do we allow the shim to rewrite model hints? e.g., v1 had `model: x-small` and v2 uses `profile: low-latency`. Mapping table?
alex: Yes, mapping table is configurable per-tenant. But default is identity. Only map if tenant opted into the shim mappings.
lia: Testing matrix: streaming integrity, large message resume, reconnect semantics, error mapping, trace continuity, perf under burst, and TLS termination checks.
shilpa: How long do we intend to keep the shim? finite window or indefinite compatibility layer?
alex: Short-lived, targeted to the migration window (~3 months after initial canary). We'll log per-tenant usage and set a hard deprecation schedule communicated to customers.
marta: Ops concerns: additional hop increases connection counts. We need autoscale policies and connection recycling to avoid FD exhaustion.
kevin: Add connection pooling + keepalive tuning. Also a circuit breaker for high-error tenants.
infra-bot: deploy-plan: create canary stack in staging -> perf test job -> rollout wave 0 (5 tenants) -> 24h monitor -> ramp 20%/50%/100% over 7 days. kill-switch implemented via feature-flag (FF) in control plane.
alex: Next steps: I'll draft an RFC with architecture sketches and perf targets, add a sample shim config, and propose rollout dates. Who wants to review?
marta: I'll take a pass on the config and error mapping matrix.
kevin: I'll own perf tests and SLO verification.
shilpa: I'll review security and token flow.
lia: I'll add the telemetry checklist and rollout alerts.
alex: Thanks all — I'll post the RFC draft into #architecture tomorrow and link this thread. :thumbsup:
